metadata.title: Palo Alto Surges Nearly 11% as AI Defense Meets a 5% Operating Margin

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
A widening AI-security opportunity pulled investors toward Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ:PANW), the network and cloud-security company, Monday as cybersecurity names rallied on fresh AI-safety concerns. Shares climbed approximately 10.8% to $366.315, based on the updated market quote, strengthening the case that investors are treating cybersecurity as one of the more durable beneficiaries of the AI spending cycle.
Palo Alto's fourth-quarter numbers give that enthusiasm some operating support. Revenue rose 34% to $3.41 billion, while next-generation security annual recurring revenue reached $9.10 billion. The company also reported $172 million of GAAP operating income versus roughly $1 billion on an adjusted basis. Meanwhile, its Frontier AI Critical Defense Program is aimed at protecting critical infrastructure at the network layer while traditional software vulnerabilities are being fixed, giving Palo Alto another route into the rapidly expanding AI-security budget.
The valuation is where the story gets much tougher. The chart shows Palo Alto at $366.315 versus a GF Value estimate of $232.09, leaving the shares 57.83% above GF Value. That premium says investors are already paying heavily for future growth. With GAAP operating margin still around 5%, the next leg higher will likely require more than rising cybersecurity demand: Palo Alto needs to show that acquisitions, platform expansion and AI-security spending can translate into stronger reported profitability as well.
